text.insert: Sync is the operator-initiated intake-and-reconciliation workflow: one manual entry point that checks for merged upstream PRs, processes their evidence, and processes any staged corpora such as Discord. New upstream PRs can invalidate local assumptions, duplicate matches, and create source conflicts, so they are observed and queued immediately but reconciled only once sync holds the dispatch lease. Conflict resolution therefore happens once at a named boundary — including applying conflicting upstream changes into the active working session — instead of leaking into running or PR workers. A sync with no upstream movement is a knowledge-only pass: it publishes staged corpus knowledge and leaves the source baseline untouched.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-11) — knowledge intake folds into sync

text.insert: There is no standalone knowledge_intake workflow kind; run, pr, and sync are the only workflow kinds that may hold the dispatch lease. Every knowledge source other than always-on worker-result evidence is processed inside an operator-started sync.
Knowledge Sources and Sync Intake
Worker-result evidence is the only always-on knowledge input, and the background sink ingests it continuously:
Every other source — newly merged upstream PRs, staged corpora such as Discord, and all remaining knowledge sources — is processed only inside an operator-started sync rather than on a schedule.
Intake that changes the executable source baseline is itself syncing, so this single manual entry point prevents the same merged-PR evidence from entering through two competing routes.
When sync starts, it checks for upstream movement while processing merged-PR evidence and staged corpora:
If merged PRs conflict with local work, sync applies the upstream changes into the active working session and completes that application before publishing.
With no upstream movement, the same entry point becomes a knowledge-only pass that does not advance the source baseline.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — sync reconciles in staging and publishes atomically

text.insert: Sync never mutates the session worktree in place; reconciliation occurs in an isolated staging workspace. One atomic publish step advances the session head, records the remote-application boundary, marks invalidations, and pushes reconciled PR branches.
Staging and the Atomic Publish

All reconciliation happens in the isolated staging workspace: the session history is rebased onto the new upstream, conflicts are resolved, and the reconciled state is revalidated before any head advances. In the typical mid-run flow, the run pauses, upstream is pulled down, reconciliation completes in staging, and only then do the heads advance.
Staging makes every pre-publish decision recoverable without disturbing the active session:
Before publish, cancelling is free: staging is discarded, the session remains exactly as it was, and "Not today" stays available as an operator answer.
If sync crashes before publish, recovery can instead resume from the last durable stage or discard staging.
Publish closes that recovery window; afterward there is no abort, and the system can only move forward.
The same staging boundary reconciles the open PR campaign's series alongside the session history:
Most series rebase cleanly; agents handle the minor merge-conflict resolution that some series require inside staging, and minor mechanical conflicts auto-resolve.
Any conflict the agents cannot resolve confidently blocks sync for operator resolution, so nothing ambiguous publishes without the operator.
The atomic publish then advances the heads and pushes the reconciled branches to their upstream PRs as one boundary.
